children: Server maker Super Micro Computer Inc. (SMCI, Financials), which supplies infrastructure for AI and data centers, is offering investors a rare configuration.
Shares slid 3.1 percent to $35.62 in the previous trading session and are down around 4 percent in the past month. The corporate outlook is considerably different.
Analysts estimate Supermicro to announce quarterly revenue of $14.77 billion, a roughly 194% increase from a year earlier. Earnings are estimated at $1.06 a share, up more than 200%.
The Street sees $67.12 billion in revenue for the whole fiscal year, up roughly 72%, and earnings of $4.43 a share. But investors aren't giving a premium for those numbers.
Supermicro's price-to-forward earnings ratio is around 8.3, below the industry average of about 10.9. The stock's PEG ratio is 0.63, likewise considerably below the industry average of 1.44.
That's the interesting part of the next earnings report.
Wall Street is already seeking high growth. Now Supermicro has to show that those sales gains can transfer into the earnings and performance investors want to see.
If it does, the current valuation difference may be harder for the market to ignore.

title: Super Micro stock slips as investors look past massive growth estimates
